title: Chapter 14. Vamshidasa, Nayanananda, Shivananda, Yadu, Govinda and Vasu Ghosha, Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa and Others: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Completing the "GPT Only" Group
html:
This chapter completes the group of padas by poets other than Narahari that are known from the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. The padas follow the order of the lilas: mangalacharana and praise of the Gaura-avatara, Gaura's form, the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and the adhivasa of the kirtana of the "seven groups," Gaura with Gauridasa in the bhava of Krishna and of Radha, the goshtha-bhava and the festival of colours, the decision to take sannyasa and the lament after it, the Ratha-yatra in Puri, Nityananda (His marriage — in a pada that Majumdar considers a forgery — His dance and His mercy), Ramananda Raya. Seven padas are signed "Yadu" (nos. 4, 5, 20–23, 26); five of them are also in the Padakalpataru (PK 2459, 2460, 1546, 1547, 2300; and PK 1548 without signature, no. 23) — there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; who this "Yadu" is — Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord, or the later Yadunandana — is not established. Checking against the text of GPT1 showed that the stage-1 catalogue had ascribed to Vamshi, Gauridasa, Paramananda and Narahari a good many padas of other poets: of the seven padas of "Vamshi," six belong to others (Vaishnava Dasa, Premadasa, Rajavallabha, Govinda Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, or are unsigned); instead, a goshtha-pada of Vamshidasa (no. 15) is translated, and the pada "āhā mari kothā gela gorā kām̐cā sonā" (no. 19 — "Vamshi" in the catalogue) is signed by Vasu Ghosha; the padas of "Gauridasa" are signed by Jagannatha Dasa and Chaitanyadasa, those of "Paramananda" by Vrindavana Dasa and Gopala Dasa. Four padas (nos. 9, 17, 23, 26) were missing from the catalogue. Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; the attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional (C; D only where authenticity itself is in doubt: an added signature, a forgery). The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Vamshidasa — "jaya re jaya re mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (GPT1 p. 5, no. 8)

Mangalacharana: glory to Gauranga, to Nityananda and to Gaura's devotees; the poet asks Sitanatha — Advaita Acharya — to give him the shade of His feet and to keep his wicked mind there: he has no other hope. Raga kamoda.1

জয় রে জয় রে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
জয় নিত্যানন্দ চন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ সীতানাথে দেহ পদছায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

jaya re jaya re mora gaurāṅga rāya |
jaya nityānanda candra jaya gaurabhaktabṛnda sītānāthe deha padachāya || dhru ||

jaya re — glory; mora — to my; gaurāṅga rāya — Gauranga Raya; nityānanda candra — Nityananda the moon; gaura-bhakta-bṛnda — the host of Gaura's devotees; sītānāthe — O Sitanatha (Sita's husband, Advaita); deha — give; pada-chāya — the shade of the feet

1.1Glory, glory to my Gauranga Raya! Glory to Nityananda the moon, glory to Gaura's devotees! Sitanatha, give me the shade of Your feet!

জয় জয় মোর আচার্য ঠাকুর অগতি পতিত অতি ।
করুণা করিয়া স্বচরণে রাখ এ মোর পাপিষ্ঠ মতি ॥

jaya jaya mora ācārya ṭhākura agati patita ati |
karuṇā kariyā svacaraṇe rākha e mora pāpiṣṭha mati ||

jaya jaya — glory, glory; mora ācārya ṭhākura — to my Acharya Thakura; agati — helpless; patita ati — utterly fallen (am I); karuṇā kariyā — being merciful; sva-caraṇe — at Your own feet; rākha — keep; e mora — this my; pāpiṣṭha mati — sinful mind

1.2Glory, glory to my Acharya Thakura! I am helpless, utterly fallen:
be merciful — keep this sinful mind of mine at Your feet.2

তোমার চরণে ভরসা কেবল না দেখি আর উপায় ।
মোর দুষ্ট মনে রাখ শ্রীচরণে এই মাগোঁ তুয়া পায় ॥

tomāra caraṇe bharasā kebala nā dekhi āra upāya |
mora duṣṭa mane rākha śrīcaraṇe ei māgom̐ tuyā pāya ||

tomāra caraṇe — in Your feet; bharasā kebala — only trust; nā dekhi — I do not see; āra upāya — another way; mora duṣṭa mane — my wicked mind; rākha śrī-caraṇe — keep at the holy feet; ei māgom̐ — this I beg; tuyā pāya — at Your feet

1.3In Your feet alone I trust — I see no other way;
keep my wicked mind at Your holy feet — this I beg at Your feet.

সদা মনোরথ যে কিছু আমার সকল জানহ তুমি ।
কহে বংশীদাস পূর সব আশ কি আর কহিব আমি ॥

sadā manoratha ye kichu āmāra sakala jānaha tumi |
kahe baṃśīdāsa pūra saba āśa ki āra kahiba āmi ||

sadā manoratha — constant desires; ye kichu āmāra — whatever is mine; sakala jānaha tumi — You know all; kahe baṃśīdāsa — says Vamshidasa; pūra saba āśa — fulfil all hopes; ki āra kahiba āmi — what more shall I say

1.4Whatever I long for at all times — all of it You know.
Says Vamshidasa: fulfil all my hopes — what more shall I say?

GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 8. The pada is not in PK, the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS) (catalogue: VV-001). Under the signature "Vamshi, Vamshidasa" there are padas of Vamshivadana Thakura, the Lord's associate, and of a later Vamshidasa (by Majumdar, PK 2851 is his; see chapter 6, no. 16); this pada is a prayer with no sign of an eyewitness; attribution by GPT (C). Vamshivadana lived with Shachi and Vishnupriya in Navadvipa (according to tradition); a prayer to Advaita is possible from him, but the pada may also belong to a disciple of Advaita's line.

2. Nayanananda — "gorā mora guṇera sāgara…" (GPT1 p. 31, no. 15)

Praise of Gaura in images: He is an ocean of virtues where waves of prema rise; a spotless moon pouring the nectar of the holy name; the Himalayan peak from which the Ganga of prema flows; a wish-fulfilling tree; a new cloud that cools everyone; a mine of bliss. Raga dhanashi.3

গোরা মোর গুণের সাগর ।
প্রেমের তরঙ্গ তায় উঠে নিরন্তর ॥

gorā mora guṇera sāgara |
premera taraṅga tāya uṭhe nirantara ||

gorā mora — my Gora; guṇera sāgara — an ocean of virtues; premera taraṅga — waves of prema; tāya — in it; uṭhe — rise; nirantara — without cease

2.1My Gora is an ocean of virtues:
in it waves of prema rise without cease.

গোরা মোর অকলঙ্ক শশী ।
হরিনাম-সুধা তাহে ক্ষরে দিবানিশি ॥

gorā mora akalaṅka śaśī |
harināma-sudhā tāhe kṣare dibāniśi ||

akalaṅka śaśī — a spotless moon; harināma-sudhā — the nectar of Hari's name; tāhe — from it; kṣare — drips; dibāniśi — day and night

2.2My Gora is a spotless moon:
day and night the nectar of Hari's name drips from it.

গোরা মোর হিমাদ্রি-শেখর ।
তাহা হৈতে প্রেম-গঙ্গা বহে নিরন্তর ॥

gorā mora himādri-śekhara |
tāhā haite prema-gaṅgā bahe nirantara ||

himādri-śekhara — the peak of the Himalayas; tāhā haite — from it; prema-gaṅgā — the Ganga of prema; bahe — flows; nirantara — without cease

2.3My Gora is the peak of the Himalayas:
from it the Ganga of prema flows without cease.

গোরা মোর প্রেম-কল্পতরু ।
যার পদচ্ছায়ে জীব সুখে বাস করু ॥

gorā mora prema-kalpataru |
yāra padacchāye jība sukhe bāsa karu ||

prema-kalpataru — the wish-fulfilling tree of prema; yāra pada-chāye — in the shade of whose feet; jība — living beings; sukhe — happily; bāsa karu — dwell

2.4My Gora is a wish-fulfilling tree that gives prema:
in the shade of His feet living beings dwell happily.

গোরা মোর নব জলধর ।
বরষি শীতল যাহে করে নারী-নর ॥

gorā mora naba jaladhara |
baraṣi śītala yāhe kare nārī-nara ||

naba jaladhara — a new rain-cloud; baraṣi — raining; śītala kare — cools; yāhe — by which; nārī-nara — women and men

2.5My Gora is a new rain-cloud:
pouring rain, He cools men and women.

গোরা মোর আনন্দের খনি ।
নয়নানন্দের প্রাণ যাহার নিছনি ॥

gorā mora ānandera khani |
nayanānandera prāṇa yāhāra nichani ||

ānandera khani — a mine of bliss; nayanānandera prāṇa — Nayanananda's life; yāhāra — for whom; nichani — a ransom offered for the beloved

2.6My Gora is a mine of bliss:
Nayanananda's life is given for Him as a ransom.4

no. 15. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: NN-003). Nayanananda Mishra is the nephew and disciple of Gadadhara Pandita; his padas on Gaura in PK were translated in chapters 4 and 10. This pada is known only from the GPT (C). him: the poet gives his life for Gaura. In 2.1 GPT1 has "guṇera nāgara" (a misprint or misreading), GPT2 "guṇera sāgara": the image of an ocean with waves requires "sagara."

3. Shivananda — "akhila bhubana bhari hari-rasa-bādara…" (GPT1 p. 35, no. 25)

The cloud of Chaitanya: a downpour of Hari's rasa has filled the universe, and the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and ask for more; the cloud was born on the full moon of Phalguna and flooded high and low with prema; the holy name became the maha-mantra, prema was given out by handfuls, the fallen became bhagavatas, Jagai and Madhai were saved; the poet laments that he has remained in forgetfulness. Raga mangala.5

অখিল ভুবন ভরি হরি-রস-বাদর বরিখয়ে চৈতন্য-মেঘে ।
ভকত চাতক যত পিবি পিবি অবিরত অনুখন প্রেম-জল মাগে ॥

akhila bhubana bhari hari-rasa-bādara barikhaye caitanya-meghe |
bhakata cātaka yata pibi pibi abirata anukhana prema-jala māge ||

akhila bhubana bhari — filling the whole universe; hari-rasa-bādara — the downpour of Hari's rasa; barikhaye — pours; caitanya-meghe — from the cloud Chaitanya; bhakata — devotees; cātaka — chataka birds; yata — all; pibi pibi — drinking and drinking; abirata — without end; anukhana — every moment; prema-jala — the water of prema; māge — beg

3.1Filling the universe, a downpour of Hari's rasa pours from the cloud of Chaitanya; the devotees, like chataka birds, drink and drink without end, every moment begging for the water of prema.

ফাল্গুন-পূর্ণিমা তিথি মেঘের জনম তথি সেই মেঘে করল বাদর ।
উচা নীচ যত ছিল প্রেম-জলে ভাসাওল গোরা বড় দয়ার সাগর ॥

phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi meghera janama tathi sei meghe karala bādara |
ucā nīca yata chila prema-jale bhāsāola gorā baṛa dayāra sāgara ||

phālguna-pūrṇimā tithi — the lunar day of the full moon of Phalguna; meghera janama — the cloud's birth; tathi — on that (day); sei meghe — that cloud; karala bādara — made a downpour; ucā nīca — high and low; yata chila — as many as there were; prema-jale — with the water of prema; bhāsāola — flooded; gorā baṛa dayāra sāgara — Gora is a great ocean of mercy

3.2The full moon of Phalguna is the cloud's birthday; that cloud poured the downpour:
high and low — it flooded all with the water of prema: Gora is a great ocean of mercy.

জীবেরে করিয়া যন্ত্র হরিনাম মহামন্ত্র হাতে হাতে প্রেমের অঞ্জলি ।
অধম দুঃখিত যত তারা হৈল ভাগবত বাঢ়িল গৌরাঙ্গ-ঠাকুরালি ॥

jībere kariyā yantra harināma mahāmantra hāte hāte premera añjali |
adhama duḥkhita yata tārā haila bhāgabata bāṛhila gaurāṅga-ṭhākurāli ||

jībere kariyā yantra — making living beings a yantra; harināma mahāmantra — Hari's name the great mantra; hāte hāte — from hand to hand; premera añjali — handfuls of prema; adhama — the low; duḥkhita — the wretched; yata — all; tārā haila bhāgabata — they became bhagavatas; bāṛhila — grew; gaurāṅga-ṭhākurāli — Gauranga's glory (lordship)

3.3Making living beings His yantra and Hari's name the maha-mantra, He gave prema by handfuls from hand to hand; all the low and wretched became bhagavatas — so Gauranga's glory grew.6

জগাই মাধাই ছিল তারা প্রেমে উদ্ধারিল হেন জীবে বিলাওল দয়া ।
দাস শিবানন্দ বলে কেন রৈনু মায়া-ভোলে প্রভু মোরে দেহ পদছায়া ॥

jagāi mādhāi chila tārā preme uddhārila hena jībe bilāola dayā |
dāsa śibānanda bale kena rainu māyā-bhole prabhu more deha padachāyā ||

jagāi mādhāi chila — there were Jagai and Madhai; tārā preme uddhārila — them He delivered with prema; hena — such; jībe — to living beings; bilāola dayā — distributed mercy; dāsa śibānanda bale — says Shivananda-dasa; kena rainu — why did I remain; māyā-bhole — in the forgetfulness of maya; prabhu — Lord; more deha pada-chāyā — give me the shade of the feet

3.4There were Jagai and Madhai — them too He saved with prema: such mercy He showed to living beings. Says Shivananda-dasa: why have I remained in the forgetfulness of maya? Lord, give me the shade of Your feet!7

PS. In the catalogue (SS-001) the first line was wrong: "iha kaliyuga dhana nityānanda caitanya" is the preceding GPT pada (no. 24), signed by Haridasa; the pada signed "dāsa śibānanda" is no. 25. Whether this is Shivananda Sena, the father of Kavi Karnapura, is unclear (C); Majumdar considers Shivananda Sena the author of padas on the Lord composed in His lifetime. diagram and a mantra serve worship, so living beings became the Lord's vessel and Hari's name the great mantra. The sense of the line is not quite clear. A footnote in GPT1 gives "durgata" (distressed) for "duḥkhita" (wretched). "Glory" (ṭhākurāli) — the Lord's majesty, lordship. everyday sense — forgetting God and attachment to the world; it has nothing to do with the Lord.

4. Yadu — "eke se kanayā-kaṣila tanu…" (PK 2459; GPT1 p. 120, no. 27)

Gauranga's form: His body like gold tested on the touchstone, outshining the moon; curls tied in a knot, garments of red silk; raising His arms He stretches — and lightning seems to flash; the gaze slips over His body, over which waves run; all pride is broken. Raga "the same" (in GPT1, "yatharaga").8

একে সে কনয়া-কষিল তনু ।
শশী-নিকলঙ্ক-দমন জনু ॥

eke se kanayā-kaṣila tanu |
śaśī-nikalaṅka-damana janu ||

eke — first of all; se — that; kanayā-kaṣila — gold tested on the touchstone; tanu — body; śaśī-nikalaṅka — the spotless moon; damana — subduing; janu — as if

4.1First of all, His body, like gold tested on the touchstone:
as if it subdues even the spotless moon.

তাহাতে লোটন চাঁচর কেশে ।
মাতায় রঙ্গিণী সুষমা-লেশে ॥

tāhāte loṭana cām̐cara keśe |
mātāya raṅgiṇī suṣamā-leśe ||

tāhāte — besides; loṭana — a knot (of hair); cām̐cara keśe — with curly locks; mātāya — intoxicates; raṅgiṇī — playful fair ones; suṣamā-leśe — with a trace of beauty

4.2And then — the curly locks tied in a knot:
even a trace of that beauty intoxicates the playful fair ones.9

কিবা অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ-শোভা ।
এ-তিন-ভুবন-রঙ্গিণী-লোভা ॥

kibā aparūpa gaurāṅga-śobhā |
e-tina-bhubana-raṅgiṇī-lobhā ||

kibā aparūpa — how wondrous; gaurāṅga-śobhā — Gauranga's beauty; e tina bhubana — of the three worlds; raṅgiṇī — of the fair ones; lobhā — coveted

4.3How wondrous is Gauranga's beauty —
coveted by the fair women of the three worlds!

অরুণ পাটের বসন ছলে ।
তরুণী-হৃদয়-রাগ উছলে ॥

aruṇa pāṭera basana chale |
taruṇī-hṛdaya-rāga uchale ||

aruṇa pāṭera basana — garment of red silk; chale — in the guise of; taruṇī-hṛdaya-rāga — the red (passion) of young hearts; uchale — overflows

4.4In the guise of His red silk garment
the red passion of young hearts seems to overflow.

বাহু উঠাইয়া মোড়য়ে তনু ।
ছটায় বিজুরী ঝলকে জনু ॥

bāhu uṭhāiyā moṛaye tanu |
chaṭāya bijurī jhalake janu ||

bāhu uṭhāiyā — raising the arms; moṛaye tanu — stretches the body; chaṭāya — in the radiance; bijurī — lightning; jhalake — flashes; janu — as if

4.5Raising His arms, He stretches His whole body —
and in its radiance lightning seems to flash.

পিছলে লোচন চাহিলে অঙ্গ ।
তনুতে তনুতে তরঙ্গ-রঙ্গ ॥

pichale locana cāhile aṅga |
tanute tanute taraṅga-raṅga ||

pichale — slips; locana — the gaze; cāhile aṅga — when one looks at the body; tanute tanute — all over the body; taraṅga-raṅga — the play of waves

4.6The gaze cast upon His body slips off:
over all His body waves run in play.

কেশর-কুসুম-সুষম-দাম ।
যদু কহে সব ভাঙ্গল মান ॥

keśara-kusuma-suṣama-dāma |
yadu kahe saba bhāṅgala māna ||

keśara-kusuma — of keshara flowers; suṣama-dāma — a lovely garland; yadu kahe — says Yadu; saba — all; bhāṅgala — is broken; māna — pride (the beloved's offended pride)

4.7A lovely garland of keshara flowers —
says Yadu: all pride is broken.10

printed p. 26); in PK the pada stands among the gaura-chandrikas to the description of beauty (before it, Premadasa's PK 2458; after it, PK 2460 and the description of Radha's beauty, "atha śrīrādhāyāṃ yathā"). GPT1 — p. 120, section on Gaura's form, no. 27 ("yatharaga"), scan PDF p. 379; GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 27. The pada is not in BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: YD-008). The signature "yadu" (Yadu) may belong to Yadunatha Kavichandra, a contemporary of the Lord (M-1961 ascribes to him padas on Gaura's bhavas), or to the later poet Yadunandana Dasa (17th c.); PK 2459–2460 show no sign of an eyewitness; C. the language of nagari-bhava (Gaura as nagara); we translate faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone for the description of the beauty of Radha and Krishna, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly feeling. "Knot" (loṭana) — hair gathered in a knot; "cām̐cara keśa" — curly locks. (or kadamba). "Pride is broken" (bhāṅgala māna) — "mana," the beloved's offended pride, melts before Gaura's beauty. PK manuscripts: "ka" — "chāla," "uchāla," "araṅga" for "chale," "uchale," "taraṅga"; "kha, gha, cha" — "madana" for "damana" (4.1: "subdues Madana").

5. Yadu — "bikaca kanayā-kamala-kām̐ti…" (PK 2460; GPT1 p. 120, no. 28)

Gauranga's form and bhava: the lustre of a full-blown golden lotus, a face like the full moon, teeth like pomegranate seeds, lips redder than the bandhuli; He walks intoxicated with an unknown rasa, with the gait of a king of elephants; tears flow from His reddish eyes; remembering His former love He weeps, thundering like a new cloud, and calls: "Where is Gadadhara?" Raga "the same."11

বিকচ কনয়া-কমল-কাঁতি ।
বদন পূর্ণিমা-চাঁদের ভাতি ॥
